title: 2k/3 How to make Arabic display correctly

posts.author: samueljackson
posts.body: i hope there's a solution for this, because rpg maker 2003 is kinda bad with arabic apparently. it displays text as pure gibberish, both in-engine and in-game, and i wonder if there's some workaround to get it to display properly, let alone get it to display right-to-left. i'm trying to make an arabic game. would this fix itself if i downloaded an arabic font? if i imported the text rather than typed it in-engine? do i need to use maniacs? i don't know, throw all of the solutions at me! i have time to try them all out.

posts.author: samueljackson
posts.body: (i dont know why i said i'm making a game, it's more of a language patch for an existing game. sorry lol)

posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
I'm afraid non-Latin character sets are very problematic with RM2k3 (it's not even using Unicode, it's based on a pretty old program), and you can just
forget
about RTL scripts, let alone ones that use ligatures (such as Arabic)... I'm sorry!

posts.author: Akkari
posts.body:
I guess the best solution then would be to use either use a bunch of Pictures or make a Tile based Font and use the sprite sheet function of the picture command to display each character individually at the exact positions you want them(if you need more Picture Slots, then yes, Maniacs would be of help here).
This would certainly be tedious, and take some time, but unless someone else has an alternative, this seems like the best solution to this issue for RPG Maker 2003. Well, that or just remaking the entire game in another engine, but not sure if that would be any less tedious and time consuming lol.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
I tried analyzing it by importing the Courier.fon font into the language, and it's clear that the corresponding characters can be easily mapped. But I'm not sure if the characters that come before the space character at
0x20
will be accessible, because that would require changing the font in the editor as well.
From what I've seen of the keyboard, it seems that those characters before the spacebar aren't used very often, or they require a key combination to access them.
Another problem is the writing direction, which is different, just like in Hebrew, which is from right to left, so it would be necessary to create an external text editor that can convert and align with spaces. The work might not be worth it...
